authorial_core.subject: A fictional woman guided by the supplied portrait, investigating a cold-store receiving record.
authorial_core.setting: A cold-storage receiving office with a ledger, CRT television and VHS playback deck.
authorial_core.event: Her shipment comparison pauses when the recorded crate number belongs to cargo with a human-shaped silhouette.
visual_priorities: The reference-guided woman interrupts her writing and looks toward the CRT, making the discovery a present human moment.
The paper 23 / CRATE entry and the large 23 tag on the recorded parcel connect the ordinary administrative record to an unsettling visual mismatch.
The human-shaped wrapped parcel is enclosed in a paused warehouse recording on physical CRT glass, with tape artifacts confined to the recorded image.
Face, screen and ledger remain simultaneously large and readable, with living skin separated from flat monochrome video.
authorial_core.baseline_prompt_en: An analog-horror photograph of an unsettling recorded moment in a cold-storage receiving office, with a woman whose face and short black bob with wispy bangs follow the supplied reference portrait. Use the portrait as visible face and hair guidance. The scene is a fictional investigation of facility records. She has pulled the receiving ledger close to an aging CRT television and VHS deck to check a shipment, and the photograph catches her interrupted comparison. Her left index finger rests directly beside the ledger entry '23 / CRATE'; her right hand holds a pen just above that same row, its nib suspended before the next mark. Her elbows stay comfortably beside her torso, and her forearms rest on the broad desk. Her gaze has moved from the entry toward the screen, her lips slightly parted, her composed face tightening at what the record reveals. A dusty sage work shirt with a loose open collar and softly rolled sleeves keeps her presence intimate and unforced. On the large CRT, a paused monochrome warehouse recording shows a tall parcel bound in cloudy translucent stretch-wrap standing upright among low wooden food crates. The parcel has a tied oval top and paired shoulder bulges, an unmistakably human-shaped silhouette. A dark vertical recess at the head appears directed toward the surveillance lens. Its large white cargo tag reads '23', visibly linking the recorded shape to the ordinary crate entry beneath her finger. A horizontal tracking tear cuts across the lower monitor image, with fine scanlines, a small blocky time counter, and a washed-out PAUSE indicator confined to the glowing glass. A VHS cassette marked NIGHT RECEIVING lies halfway inside the deck. The physical office remains tangible: dented gray steel cabinetry, paper edges, scratched laminate and a frosted interior window. Frame the scene as a horizontal medium-close photograph from the desk's front-left corner, keeping her three-quarter face on the left, the CRT on the right, and the tilted ledger large in the lower foreground. The face, two-digit tag, finger contact and corresponding ledger entry are simultaneously clear at this intimate viewing distance. Cool CRT spill and a small tungsten desk lamp separate her living skin from the flat archived image. Slightly muted photographic color and fine grain support a quiet, credible discovery whose threat emerges through the trusted recording and its administrative mismatch.
